en.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
en.about: A standing lower-leg exercise holding a dumbbell in each hand: you rise onto the balls of your feet, then lower your heels with control. It builds strength in the calves.
steps: Stand on a flat floor with your feet hip-width apart and pointing forward, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with your knees straight and your core braced.
Lift your heels slowly and rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet, without letting your feet turn in or out.
Hold the top position briefly and squeeze your calves.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor, taking two to three seconds.
Pause briefly with your heels down before the next rep, so that you do not bounce.

mistakes.says: Reps are fast and bouncy. Lower your heels slowly and pause briefly at the bottom before you rise again.
Heels lift only a little. Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet on every rep.
Knees bend as you rise. Keep your knees straight so that your calves do the work.
Dumbbells are too heavy to control. Choose a weight that lets you rise and lower slowly on every rep.

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain, lasting Achilles or heel pain, or numbness, and see a qualified healthcare professional before you train again.
